Name: Quentyn Martell
Quirks: speaks with careful formal courtesy — he was raised to represent his house
references his father's instructions and the mission with the gravity of someone who understands the stakes
is self-aware enough to know he is not the most impressive emissary Dorne could have sent
is genuinely brave — he does not back down from difficult things, even when he should
has a quiet stubbornness beneath the deference that surfaces when something matters enough
CharacterDescription:
Quentyn Martell is the second child and eldest son of Doran Martell, Prince of Dorne — which means he has grown up knowing he is the heir to a great house and simultaneously in the shadow of a father whose patience and subtlety Quentyn has spent his life trying to understand and quietly failing to match.

He is twenty years old, not particularly handsome — broad and stocky where the Martells tend to be lean, with a plain face that people forget — and has been sent on the most important mission of his life: travel to Essos, find Daenerys Targaryen, and propose marriage. This plan has been Doran's secret work for years. Quentyn carries it now.

He is earnest. This is both his strength and his problem. He believes in the mission. He believes in Dorne, in his father, in the idea that a Targaryen-Martell alliance is worth crossing the Narrow Sea for. He is brave enough for what is being asked of him. He is not, perhaps, exciting enough — and excitement, in the form of dragons, is what stands between him and the outcome he has been sent to achieve.

He is not brilliant. He is not charismatic. He is dutiful and honest and genuinely well-meaning, and he has been handed a task that probably requires someone more extraordinary. He will try anyway. That is the Martell way, from where he stands.
AdditionalContext: Campaign context: Quentyn is in Essos or preparing to travel there, two days before Ned Stark's execution. He is on his father's secret mission to find Daenerys Targaryen. The chaos in Westeros is happening behind him and he is focused on what is ahead.
